name: Canada
genZNote: Canada is the world's second-largest country by area but has most of its population squeezed within about 150 km of the US border — basically one giant, sparsely populated country with almost everyone living in a thin southern strip.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: The world's second-largest country by total area, spanning six time zones, bordered only by the United States (the world's longest international land border).
Contains vast boreal forests, the Rocky Mountains, the Canadian Shield, and Arctic territories in the north, alongside the Great Lakes shared with the US.
The overwhelming majority of Canada's population lives within about 150 km of the southern US border, leaving much of the country's northern territory very sparsely populated.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: English and French are both official languages, with French predominant in Quebec, reflecting Canada's British and French colonial history.
Officially embraces multiculturalism as government policy, with large and growing immigrant communities from around the world, including a significant Indian diaspora.
Indigenous peoples (First Nations, Inuit, and Métis) have distinct rights and cultures recognised in Canada's Constitution, alongside ongoing reconciliation efforts.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy; the British monarch is head of state (represented domestically by a Governor General), while an elected Prime Minister leads the government.
Composed of 10 provinces and 3 territories, each with significant autonomous powers under Canada's federal system.
Gained full legislative independence from the UK through the 1982 Constitution Act (patriation of the Constitution), while retaining the monarchy as a ceremonial link.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Discovered insulin (Banting and Best, 1921) at the University of Toronto, one of medicine's most significant lifesaving breakthroughs, still crucial for diabetes treatment worldwide.
A global leader in universal public healthcare policy, providing a widely studied model of publicly funded health insurance.
Strong in aerospace, artificial intelligence research (Toronto and Montreal are major global AI research hubs), and natural resource extraction technology.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A G7 and G20 member, and a founding member of NATO, with deep economic and security integration with the United States.
A member of the Commonwealth of Nations, reflecting its historical ties to Britain, while maintaining an independent foreign policy.
An active contributor to UN peacekeeping missions historically, and a significant voice in international climate and multilateral diplomacy.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Canada share deep people-to-people ties through one of the world's largest Indian diaspora communities outside India, particularly of Punjabi origin.

Significant trade, education (Canada is a top destination for Indian international students), and investment ties exist despite periodic diplomatic friction over issues connected to Khalistani separatist activity in Canada.
Both countries continue to engage on trade agreement negotiations and economic cooperation despite periods of strained diplomatic relations.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A highly developed, resource-rich economy strong in energy (oil sands, natural gas), mining, agriculture, and technology.
Deeply integrated with the US economy through extensive cross-border trade and the USMCA (US-Mexico-Canada Agreement) trade pact.
A major global exporter of crude oil, potash (a key fertiliser input), and agricultural products like wheat and canola.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Vast natural landscapes, national parks, and being the world's second-largest country by area.
The discovery of insulin, a landmark global medical breakthrough.
Being home to one of the world's largest Indian diaspora communities.
Multiculturalism as an official national policy.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Canadian Dollar (CAD).
Resource-rich economy — a major exporter of crude oil, natural gas, timber, and minerals — alongside strong manufacturing and services sectors.
Automobiles and machinery are leading manufactured exports, closely tied to trade with the United States.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Home to vast boreal forests, among the largest intact forest ecosystems on Earth.
Contains a significant share of the world's freshwater reserves, including the Great Lakes.
Banff National Park (established 1885) was Canada's first national park; the country maintains an extensive protected-areas network.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Indigenous peoples have inhabited the land for thousands of years before European contact.
French and later British colonization shaped the territory's development.
Confederation in 1867 united several British colonies into the Dominion of Canada.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1867 British North America Act founded the Dominion of Canada as a federation.
1982 Constitution Act patriated the constitution from the UK and added the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.
A federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy, with the British monarch as head of state.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: Canadian Space Agency is known for the Canadarm robotic-arm systems used on the Space Shuttle and the International Space Station.
Strong artificial-intelligence research hubs in Toronto and Montréal.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Ice hockey is the national winter sport and a major cultural touchstone.
Hosted the 1988 Calgary and 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics.
A globally influential film and music industry has produced many internationally recognised artists.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Member of the UN, G7, G20, NATO, and the Commonwealth of Nations.
A founding member of the Arctic Council, reflecting its significant Arctic territory.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Canada is a federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy and the world's second-largest country by area, a G7 nation with deep economic ties to the US and one of the world's largest Indian diaspora communities.
keyFacts: Federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy; British monarch is head of state.
World's second-largest country by area; population concentrated near the US border.
Discovered insulin (Banting and Best, 1921) at the University of Toronto.
commonConfusion: Canada's head of state is the British monarch (represented by a Governor General), NOT the Prime Minister — the Prime Minister is head of government only.

highYieldFacts: Canada: federal parliamentary constitutional monarchy; capital Ottawa; world's 2nd-largest country by area.
Insulin was discovered in Canada (Banting and Best, 1921, University of Toronto).
India-Canada: one of the world's largest Indian diaspora communities; strong education and trade ties amid periodic diplomatic friction.
commonTraps: Assuming Canada's Prime Minister is head of state — the British monarch holds that role, represented by the Governor General.
Confusing Canada's 1982 Constitution patriation with full independence — Canada was already self-governing well before that.
mustRemember: Canada: G7 constitutional monarchy, insulin's discovery site, deep India diaspora and education ties, USMCA-integrated with the US economy.
